title: Karnataka Chief Minister speaks to protesting ASHA workers from Japan, urges them to call off stir

ai.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar urged ASHA workers to withdraw their indefinite protest demanding ₹15,000 monthly honorarium and fulfillment of pending demands via video call from Japan.

facts.claim: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke to protesting ASHA workers at Bengaluru’s Freedom Park through a video call from Japan
facts.quote: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) spoke to protesting ASHA workers at Bengaluru’s Freedom Park through a video call from Japan and urged them to withdraw their agitation.

facts.claim: The Chief Minister promised to address ASHA workers' demands with the Finance Department during the Legislature session
facts.quote: During the video call, the Chief Minister said he would discuss their demands with the Finance Department during the Legislature session, as some of the issues involved other departments.

facts.claim: ASHA workers demanded ₹15,000 monthly honorarium and fulfillment of pending demands
facts.quote: Demanding that the State government fix their monthly honorarium at ₹15,000 and fulfil their pending demands, members of the Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha had launched an indefinite day-and-night protest on November 17.

facts.claim: The protest was ongoing as the Chief Minister was in Japan
facts.quote: The call came amid criticism from the protesters over his Japan visit while their agitation was under way.

ai.background_note: Karnataka ASHA workers have been protesting for over a week demanding higher honorarium and fulfillment of pending demands, with the Chief Minister's Japan visit adding political tension to the situation.
